title: Significant Water Withdrawal Facility Data
authors: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Division of Water
boundary: Aggregate withdrawal capability per facility, all sources and methods
finding: Facilities capable of withdrawing more than 100,000 gallons/day must register and report annual use. Data distinguish pump capacity from annual withdrawal. Municipal supply records do not identify every downstream data-center customer.
limitations: Retrieved page lists pump register as of August 1, 2025 and recent reported years; do not assume 2026 measured coverage. No statewide data-center-specific consumption total established.

title: Fort Wayne Google Data Center Frequently Asked Questions
authors: City of Fort Wayne; information supplied by Google, Indiana Michigan Power and City Utilities
type: Municipal FAQ incorporating corporate and utility claims
metric: Water-system average daily use and treatment capacity
boundary: Whole municipal system; NOT the Google campus
finding: Supply is the St. Joseph River. The FAQ says Google lowers non-critical electric loads during grid stress rather than substituting diesel generation.
limitations: No campus water withdrawal or consumption measurement. Treatment capacity is not a drought-yield assessment. Emissions and rate claims are attributed, not independently audited.

title: Adams Center Water Tower
finding: Google funds the planned tank and transmission infrastructure; assets become publicly owned after acceptance.
limitations: Tank volume is neither daily withdrawal nor consumption; project completion not verified.

title: Amazon's Investment Is Building Lasting Opportunity for St. Joseph County
authors: Amazon statement published by South Bend Regional Chamber of Commerce
metric: Projected annual campus water use at full buildout
geography: AWS New Carlisle, St. Joseph County, Indiana
boundary: New Carlisle site at full buildout; source does not explicitly define withdrawal versus consumption
status: Operator projection, NOT observed meter data
finding: Operator projects roughly 18 million gallons annually and outside-air cooling for 98% of the year.
limitations: Indexed primary statement retrieved; direct page access returned 403. Confirmed by corrected August reporting. No metering method, monthly series, campus WUE, return-flow balance or assured peak limit supplied.

title: Dry wells and water supply fears surround Amazon's massive Indiana data center
authors: Redmond Bernhold; Alyssa Sirichoktanasup; Andy Caron, University of Notre Dame Gallivan Program
type: Corrected original reporting; Indianapolis Star syndication
geography: AWS New Carlisle, St. Joseph County, Indiana
boundary: Construction pumping; not campus consumptive use
status: Reported authorization; dewatering source document not reviewed
finding: Corrects sewer extrapolation. Reports dry-well hardship, DNR drought attribution, and hydrologist disagreement.
limitations: Do not sum with cooling or sewer flows. Written DNR investigation report reportedly unavailable. Causation unresolved. Sewer design is now verified separately in IN15.

title: Economic Outlook: Data Centers and the Regional Economy (Season 21, Episode 1)
authors: PBS Michiana; host Jeff Rea; testimony of Bill Schalliol and other panelists
type: Public broadcast with firsthand county-official statement
metric: Combined withdrawal limit described for two public plants
boundary: All users supplied by two town-managed water-treatment plants
status: Official description of system cap; not Amazon actual use
finding: County economic development director explicitly places the 24 MGD cap at the two plants and distinguishes other users such as agricultural irrigation.
limitations: Not a campus-specific permit or metered use series. Aquifer yield numbers in different sources differ; omit a precise available-water surplus without original hydrologic model review.

title: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
finding: Microsoft commits to energy-efficient closed-loop liquid cooling; first phase expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs.
limitations: Does not provide observed withdrawal, consumptive loss, WUE, power demand or lifecycle emissions. Closed-loop does not establish zero site or supply-chain water use. Exact groundbreaking date differs from some media; use June 2026 if not central.

title: Microsoft, Dermody update tax agreement to include historic funding for La Porte schools
metric: School share of tax revenue under updated agreement
boundary: Municipal fiscal agreement, not environmental performance
finding: City says Microsoft will pay full property taxes and redevelopment commission will allocate 15% of revenue to schools over 20 years.
limitations: Announcement is not an independent net fiscal-benefit evaluation; environmental costs remain separate.

title: Ordinance No. 2026-08: An ordinance establishing a development moratorium on data centers
type: Signed government ordinance; all three pages visually verified
boundary: New data-center applications in county jurisdiction; excludes existing facilities
status: Enacted; scheduled active on review date
finding: Adopted June 15, 2026. Section 2 commences June 16, 2026; section 3 ends June 15, 2027. Applies to new data-center applications in unincorporated Boone County.
limitations: Signed primary instrument supersedes the anomalous announcement URL. No subsequent repeal located in targeted search.

title: Data Centers
status: Enacted; scheduled active on review date
finding: One-year pause; town identifies infrastructure, utilities, traffic, noise and neighborhood compatibility as study topics.
limitations: Not a Lake County-wide or Indiana-wide ban. No repeal located in reviewed source.

title: Ordinance imposing a temporary moratorium on the development of data centers
boundary: Applications and permits for data-center structures and appurtenant facilities
status: Historical moratorium; subsequent ordinance reported adopted July 20
finding: Recorded ordinance imposed a pause without a calendar expiry, ending when the zoning ordinance gains data-center regulations.
limitations: Must read with IN12; do not classify indefinitely active simply because May source remains online.

title: Data centers: A hot-mic conversation leads to a discussion of what government transparency means
type: Original public-radio reporting; links county minutes
boundary: County zoning regulation and community resistance
finding: Reports July 20 adoption and continuing coalition concern about transparency; cites official minutes. This supplies evidence that the temporary moratorium should not be counted as currently active.
limitations: Signed replacement ordinance not extracted; zoning standards in reporting should be checked against final text for enforcement.

title: St. Joseph County Council takes first step toward possible ban on future hyperscale data centers
status: Preliminary action; NOT an enacted ban
finding: Reports a 6–3 preliminary resolution beginning the process toward a possible future ban.
limitations: No completed ban established as of search cutoff. Report publication date differs from vote date; use September 2026 unless signed minutes are verified.

title: Will our water meet our needs?
type: Original local reporting of public presentation
boundary: Proposed data-center campus and White River watershed
finding: Documents competing assurances and resident concern; reports a conservation-district representative's prospective 8 MGD estimate.
limitations: Do not promote 8 MGD to measured use or multiply separately reported per-building maxima. Original utility contract, final phase boundary and operating data not verified.

title: Authorization for Construction of Sanitary Sewer System, IEC-3 South, Permit Approval No. 26205
authors: Indiana Department of Environmental Management, Office of Water Quality
type: Primary approved construction permit and application; permit p. 2 visually verified
metric: Design wastewater flows for sewer project
geography: AWS IEC-3 South, northwest corner Gordon Road/Strawberry Road, St. Joseph County, Indiana
boundary: Sanitary and industrial wastewater sewer project; approved description refers to a 224,000 SF data center and future 224,000 SF data center. Not whole-campus water withdrawal or consumption.
status: Approved design figures, not measured operations
finding: Permit p. 2 authorizes future average 55,000 GPD and future peak 1,612,000 GPD wastewater design flow. Treatment goes to City of South Bend.
limitations: Avoid extrapolating to campus consumption. Appendix unit counts differ in presentation from permit narrative; use permit project boundary and do not infer a campus building count. No actual flow series included.
